{{short description|Invariant of closed manifolds, in mathematics}}
{{More footnotes|date=May 2020}}
In mathematics, the '''Kervaire semi-characteristic''', introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Kervaire|first=Michel|authorlink=Michel Kervaire|year=1956}}, is an invariant of [[closed manifold]]s ''M'' of dimension <math>4n+1</math> taking values in <math>\Z/2\Z</math>, given by 

:<math>k_F(M) = \sum_{i=0}^{2n} \dim H^{2i}(M,F)\bmod 2</math> 

where F is a field.

{{harvs|txt|last1= Atiyah|first1= Michael |author1-link=Michael Atiyah|last2=Singer|first2= Isadore |author2-link=Isadore Singer|year=1971}} showed that the Kervaire semi-characteristic of a [[differentiable manifold]] is given by the [[Atiyah–Singer index theorem|index]] of a skew-adjoint [[elliptic operator]].

Assuming ''M'' is [[orientability|oriented]], the '''Atiyah vanishing theorem''' states that if ''M'' has two linearly independent [[vector field]]s, then <math>k(M) = 0</math>.<ref>{{cite book|first=Weiping|last=Zhang|title=Lectures on Chern–Weil theory and Witten deformations| series=Nankai Tracts in Mathematics|volume= 4| location= River Edge, NJ|
url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8OfUCgAAQBAJ&pg=PA105|accessdate=6 July 2018|date=2001-09-21|publisher=[[World Scientific]]| isbn=9789814490627|page=105|mr=1864735 }}</ref>

The difference <math>k_\Q(M)-k_{\Z/2}(M)</math> is the [[de Rham invariant]] of <math>M</math>.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Lusztig|first1= George |author1-link=George Lusztig|last2= Milnor|first2= John |author2-link=John Milnor|last3=Peterson|first3= Franklin P. |author3-link=Franklin P. Peterson|title=Semi-characteristics and cobordism| series=Topology|volume= 8|date=1969|publisher=[[Topology]]|page=357–359}}</ref>
